name: Nicotine
summary: The clearest demonstration in everyday pharmacology that the route matters more than the dose. The same molecule is mildly pleasant from a patch and fiercely addictive from smoke, purely because of how fast it arrives.
mechanism: Agonist at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, especially the α4β2 subtype in the ventral tegmental area, which triggers dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens. The speed of the rise is what the reward system reads: inhaled nicotine reaches the brain in about 10-20 seconds, faster than an intravenous injection, because it travels the short path from lung to left heart to brain.

smoked.note: Absorbed across the huge surface of the lung and in the arterial blood within seconds. A cigarette delivers roughly 1 to 1.5 mg systemically, far less than the 10-15 mg in the tobacco itself.

gum.note: Buccal absorption, but only if chewed slowly and parked against the cheek. Chewers typically extract 50-75% of the gum's nicotine, and whatever is swallowed is largely destroyed by first-pass metabolism.

patch.note: Transdermal, deliberately slow. It holds a flat level for 16-24 hours and produces almost no spike, which is exactly why it treats dependence without feeding it.

vaped.note: Pulmonary like smoking, though delivery varies enormously with device power, nicotine salt versus freebase, and puff pattern.

oral_pouch.note: Buccal, similar to gum but steadier since nothing depends on chewing technique.

pathways.name: Cotinine
pathways.note: Inactive, but with a 16-hour half-life, which is why it is the standard biomarker for tobacco use and shows up in tests days later.

pathways.name: Other / renal
pathways.note: Glucuronidation and unchanged renal excretion; the renal share rises when urine is acidic.

effect_levels.label: Typical level between cigarettes in a regular smoker
Acute toxicity reported in non-tolerant adults

cyp2a6_slow.note: Slow CYP2A6 metabolizers, common in East Asian populations, keep nicotine around longer, smoke fewer cigarettes and find it markedly easier to quit.

cyp2a6_fast.note: Fast metabolizers clear it quickly, feel withdrawal sooner, and smoke more often.

pregnancy.note: Clearance rises about 60% in pregnancy, so the same habit produces lower levels.

menthol.note: Menthol mildly inhibits CYP2A6 and slows nicotine clearance.

sources.text: Benowitz NL, Hukkanen J, Jacob P. Nicotine chemistry, metabolism, kinetics and biomarkers. Handb Exp Pharmacol. 2009;192:29-60.
